title: Assessing the validity of leucine zipper constructs predicted by AlphaFold.
authors: Mitic, Isobel; Rowell, Keiran; Litfin, Thomas; Michie, Katharine A; Jacques, David A
journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用AlphaFold预测AP-1转录因子亮氨酸拉链二聚体结构，评估AI结构预测在TF-DNA相关二聚化界面建模中的可信度与局限，虽未直接建模TF-DNA结合，但聚焦TF二聚化互作且方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系。
abstract: AP-1 transcription factors are a network of cellular regulators that combine in different dimer pairs to control a range of pathways involved in differentiation, growth, and cell death. They dimerize via leucine zipper coiled-coil domains that are preceded by a basic DNA binding domain. Depending on which AP-1 transcription factors dimerize, different DNA sequences will be recognized resulting in differential gene expression. The affinity of AP-1 transcription factors for each other dictates which dimers form. The relative concentration of AP-1 transcription factors varies with tissue type and environment, adding another layer of control to this integral network of cellular regulation. The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based protein structure prediction methods gives us a new technique to investigate or predict how dimerization affects combinatorial control. All versions of AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold3 are AI/deep learning programs that predict 3D structures of proteins from an amino acid sequence and multiple sequence alignments of homologous proteins. To fully realize the potential of AI for structural biology, it is essential to understand its current capabilities and limitations. In this study, we used the classical example of an AP-1 dimer: Fos and Jun, and an array of over 2000 experimentally tested human leucine zippers to interrogate how AlphaFold models leucine zipper domains and if AlphaFold can be used to differentiate between probable and improbable dimer interfaces. We found that AlphaFold predicts highly confident leucine zipper dimers, even for dimer pairs such as the FosB homodimer, for which electrostatics are known to prevent their formation in vivo. This is an important case study concerning high-confidence but low-accuracy protein structure prediction.
abstract_zh: AP-1转录因子是一类细胞调控因子网络，通过不同的二聚体配对组合来控制涉及分化、生长和细胞死亡的多种通路。它们通过亮氨酸拉链卷曲螺旋结构域进行二聚化，该结构域之前有一个碱性DNA结合域。根据哪些AP-1转录因子发生二聚化，会识别不同的DNA序列，从而导致差异基因表达。AP-1转录因子之间的亲和力决定了哪些二聚体形成。AP-1转录因子的相对浓度随组织类型和环境而变化，为这一细胞调控核心网络增加了另一层控制。基于人工智能（AI）的蛋白质结构预测方法的发展，为我们提供了一种新技术，以研究或预测二聚化如何影响组合调控。所有版本的AlphaFold2和AlphaFold3都是AI/深度学习程序，它们从氨基酸序列和同源蛋白的多序列比对中预测蛋白质的三维结构。要充分实现AI在结构生物学中的潜力，理解其当前的能力和局限性至关重要。在本研究中，我们使用AP-1二聚体的经典例子：Fos和Jun，以及超过2000个经过实验验证的人类亮氨酸拉链阵列，来探究AlphaFold如何建模亮氨酸拉链结构域，以及AlphaFold是否能用于区分可能和不可能的二聚体界面。我们发现，AlphaFold预测出高置信度的亮氨酸拉链二聚体，即使对于像FosB同源二聚体这样的配对，已知静电作用会阻止其在体内形成。这是一个关于高置信度但低准确性蛋白质结构预测的重要案例研究。
